mechanics.premise: A book-length account of the 1963 Birmingham campaign arguing that American racial justice could not be deferred.
mechanics.tone_function: The title itself states the tone's thesis: the matter cannot wait. The book is the clearest single-work statement that urgency can be a moral claim rather than a marketing device.
mechanics.time_handling: 1963 is framed as a hinge year; the narrative repeatedly converts 'someday' into 'now' by tying demands to events that have already happened.
mechanics.lexical_fields: Waiting, delay, now, hour; debt and obligation; momentum.
mechanics.syntax_and_rhythm: Declarative, sermon-inflected prose; accumulating clauses resolve into short summary sentences.
mechanics.emotional_progression: Diagnosis of delay -> evidence of harm -> moral summons; urgency is earned by documented events before it is asserted.
mechanics.verification_note: Book, author, year and subject confirmed via reference summary. Techniques described, not quoted.
